sections.name: prepare_render_manifest
sections.title: Render manifest calculation
sections.what: Checks that component identities are unique and that every position and size is a real number. It then builds a box that encloses all components, falls back to a unit box when there are none, and returns the counts, triangle total, centre, size and radius.
sections.why: Likely reason: the renderer needs a safe, valid scene summary before drawing. The unit box fallback avoids empty bounds when there is nothing to show.
sections.watch_out: Each component is treated as an unrotated box, so rotated components may extend beyond the bounds, and this should be fixed or stated before relying on the framing.

summary: Runs basic safety checks on a project model before rendering: unique component identities, finite coordinates, and a combined box and triangle total for the whole model.
purpose: Makes sure the renderer only receives a model whose components are unique and whose numbers are sound, and gives it the overall size of the scene.
why: Likely reason: a broken coordinate or duplicate identity would make the 3D view wrong or crash, so it is checked before drawing.
how: Collects the component identities and rejects duplicates. Then, for each component, reads its position and size, checks the numbers are finite, and extends a running box by the component's half-size on each axis. If the model has no components, a default unit box is used. Non-finite values stop the check. The function then computes the overall size, centre and radius, and returns the manifest.
inputs: A project model with its list of components, each with a position, dimensions and triangle budget.
outputs: A render manifest with counts, the triangle total, the bounding box, the finite flag and the abstract geometry count.
risks: The box ignores each component's rotation, so a rotated item can extend beyond the reported bounds. The abstract geometry count is always zero and does not measure anything here.
debug: If the check fails, the error says either that identities are duplicated or that coordinates are not finite. Look for the component with the bad value. If the framing looks off, check whether rotated components are outside the reported box.
